[AI engineering](../index.qmd) / Training adaptation and distillation

Understand when changing a model is justified, and how to measure whether the change transfers to unseen tasks.

## What to understand

- **Training data:** collection rights, cleaning, annotation, coverage, splits, contamination and versioning.
- **Supervised fine-tuning:** train on task demonstrations; learn full tuning versus parameter-efficient methods such as LoRA/PEFT.
- **Distillation:** use a stronger teacher’s outputs or judgments to teach a smaller student. Validate data quality and applicable usage terms.
- **Preference optimization:** preference pairs, DPO, reward modeling and reinforcement learning; these are deeper electives.
- **Training mechanics:** loss curves, overfitting, checkpoints, compute, quantization and reproducible experiments.
- **Deployment comparison:** compare the adapted model with the original on held-out quality, latency, cost and important subgroups.

## How the pieces connect

Retrieval supplies knowledge at run time; fine-tuning changes weights. Distillation is a training strategy, not a promise that a small model will retain all teacher capabilities.

## A question to test

Begin with a paper experiment design: identify a repeated failure, a dataset you may use, a baseline and a held-out test. Train only when the evidence and access justify it.

**Platform note, 25 November 2026:** OpenAI’s self-serve fine-tuning has restricted access and a retirement timeline. Learn the concepts with current tooling, and check [the official availability notice](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/deprecations) before planning a training run.
